title: charts(redwood-private): expose runtime profile pack config + override pins via values.yaml
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: - Private installs can now (a) mount a profile pack config file and (b) pin/override profile selection via Helm values, with guardrails documented. - Adds values.schema.json validation for the new knobs; defaults preserve current behavior (auto-select, no pin).
description: Motivation: The runtime profile pack is now the default tuning mechanism across Hosted/Dedicated, and Private customers have been asking for a supported way to (1) supply a vetted profile pack artifact and (2) pin a known-good profile_version/profile_id during rollout/incident mitigation. This PR exposes those knobs in the `redwood-private` Helm chart while keeping safe defaults (no pin; runtime auto-select based on detected SKU) and providing explicit guidance on which settings are supported in Private. Summary of changes: Adds `runtime.profilePack` values to mount an optional profile pack config (as a ConfigMap or existing Secret), adds `runtime.profileOverrides` to pass through supported pin/override fields to the runtime, and documents defaults + upgrade notes in the chart README. Also adds JSON schema validation and a NOTES snippet that prints the effective config source and warns when pins are set (to reduce "mystery performance changes" during support escalations). Scope/Non-goals: This PR only wires values -> env/args + mounts; it does not implement runtime selection logic (handled in `redwood` monorepo) and does not introduce per-customer bespoke profiles beyond what the profile pack already supports. Safety: The chart does not enable pins by default. When a user sets `profileVersion` or `profileId`, we require an explicit acknowledgement flag in values (`runtime.profileOverrides.allowUnsafePins=true`) unless `mode=auto` and only `profileVersion` is pinned. This is aligned with the override guardrails discussed in ENG-4936. Testing: `helm template` snapshots updated, schema validation added, and CI renders for default + pinned variants. Checklist: [x] Backwards compatible defaults [x] values.schema.json updated [x] README and values.yaml commented [x] Verified chart renders for Hosted-like and Private minimal installs [x] Linked to runtime PR that consumes these fields. Related: ENG-4936 (Dedicated/Private overrides), runtime PR redwood#24944 (introduce profile_version pin + audit hook), private installer PR redwood-private-installer#602 (warn on unsupported driver/CUDA combos).
commits: charts: add runtime.profilePack values and wire mount into deployment
schema: validate profilePack + override fields; require allowUnsafePins for hard pins
docs: update README and values.yaml comments with defaults + examples
notes: print active profile config source and pin warnings in NOTES.txt
illustrative_snippet: New values (excerpt): runtime:  profilePack:    enabled: false    source: configMap # configMap|secret|existingSecret|none    name: ""        # when source=configMap/secret, chart will create it    existingSecretName: "" # when source=existingSecret    key: "profile-pack.yaml"  profileOverrides:    mode: auto       # auto|pinned    profileVersion: "" # e.g. "1.0.0" (recommended pin)    profileId: ""      # e.g. "h100-sxm-prod-v3" (advanced)    allowUnsafePins: false  # required when setting profileId or mode=pinned
review_conversation: Noah Patel: Can we avoid exposing profileId pin by default? It’s the one that tends to create hard-to-debug mismatches when hardware detection differs from what customers think they’re running. Ethan Park (author): Agree. I added `allowUnsafePins` gating: profileId and `mode=pinned` require explicit opt-in; profileVersion pin alone is allowed without the unsafe flag (still prints a warning). Omar El-Sayed: For Private, we should be clear what we pass through: profile pack path + override pins only, not individual scheduler/memory knobs. Please add that to README; we don’t want support tickets where customers set half the knobs and blame the profile pack. Ethan: Updated README with a “Supported overrides” section and explicitly points to runtime docs for advanced tuning; chart only supports pack + pins. Sean Gallagher: Please ensure the NOTES output does not leak full file contents (some customers may store pack in a Secret). Ethan: NOTES only prints which source is configured (configMap/secret/existingSecret) and whether pins are set; no content is rendered. Kira Thompson: Add an example values block for "pin profileVersion during POC"; support keeps asking for a copy/paste snippet. Ethan: Added an example in README under “Common workflows”. Irene Choi: Minor: we should not imply driver/CUDA compatibility enforcement is in Helm. It’s runtime/installer’s job. Ethan: Adjusted wording; README now says “runtime/installer may refuse unsupported combinations” and links to installer warnings. Approvals: Noah Patel approved after gating changes; Sean Gallagher approved after NOTES verification; Omar El-Sayed approved after docs clarification.
post_merge_notes: Follow-up requested by SRE: once runtime /health includes profile_version (redwood#25014), we may want to add an optional ServiceMonitor annotation example to scrape it in Private clusters. Not included here to keep chart surface area minimal.
